title: Corner or diagonal: how much walk?
hook: East then north, or straight across the field. How much walking does the shortcut save?

knows: that a² + b² = c² for the long side of a right triangle
doesNotKnow: how much walking a diagonal saves

misconception: A diagonal is only a little shorter than the two sides added.
objective: The learner can compute a diagonal from its two legs and see that it is far shorter than going round the corner.

claims.text: Straight across 300 m east and 400 m north is √(300² + 400²) = √250000 = 500 m.
claims.source: Pythagorean theorem; recomputed in node: Math.hypot(300, 400) = 500.

claims.text: The L-route is 300 + 400 = 700 m, so straight across saves 700 − 500 = 200 m, about 29% of the walk.

For the straight side c of a right triangle with legs a and b, a² + b² = c², and c is always shorter than a + b. The stage shows east² + north² and its square root for the chosen destination, rounded to the nearest whole number and marked "about" when not exact (at the start, 100² + 200² = 50,000, and its square root is about 224, since √50,000 ≈ 223.6).
claims.source: Pythagorean theorem; (a + b)² = a² + b² + 2ab > c² for a, b > 0, so a + b > c. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 19): DISPUTED. The theorem half is fine ((a+b)^2 = c^2 + 2ab > c^2 for a,b > 0). But the stage caption says 'e^2 + n^2 = X, and its square root is S' with S = Math.round(hypot): at the starting position (100, 200) it reads '...= 50,000, and its square root is 224', yet sqrt(50,000) = 223.6. Same at (100,100) 141 vs 141.42 and most other cells; only Pythagorean cells like (300,400) are exact. Fix (builder): caption 'its square root is about S' (or use = only when exact), and match the claim text. | v2 (2026-10-14, builder): caption now says "about S" unless S² equals east² + north² exactly (e.g. 300, 400 gives exactly 500), per pass 19; claim text matches. Previous verdict void; needs re-check. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 20): Caption at Demo.tsx line 75 adds 'about ' unless S*S equals e^2+n^2. Own node: (100,200) 50,000 -> 'about 224' (223.61); (300,400) 250,000 -> '500' exact; (100,100) 'about 141'. Theorem half re-derived: (a+b)^2 = c^2 + 2ab > c^2 for a,b > 0.

claims.text: The distances assume flat ground with nothing in the way of the straight path.
claims.source: Stated on stage ('Flat ground') and in the reveal. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 19): Convention, true of the model: Demo.tsx uses Euclidean distance on a plane (Math.hypot) with no obstacles; the reveal says 'Flat ground assumed.' Source wording note: 'Flat ground' appears only in the reveal, not on the stage, and 'nothing in the way' is implied, not stated.

recall.question: You walk 60 m east then 80 m north. Straight across instead, how much shorter is the walk?
recall.why: Straight across is √(60² + 80²) = √10000 = 100 m, against 60 + 80 = 140 m: 40 m shorter.
